question: Under the Maine CDL manual, which vehicle configuration requires a Class A CDL?
choice_a: A combination vehicle with a GCWR under 20,000 pounds
choice_b: A combination of vehicles with a gross combination weight rating of 26,001 pounds or more, where the towed unit's GVWR exceeds 10,000 pounds
choice_c: A single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 pounds or more
choice_d: Any vehicle that transports hazardous materials, regardless of size
explanation: Class A is defined as any combination of vehicles with a GCWR of 26,001 pounds or more, provided the towed unit's GVWR or gross weight exceeds 10,000 pounds.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, Definitions of Classes

question: How does the manual define a Class B commercial motor vehicle?
choice_a: A combination vehicle with a GCWR of 26,001 pounds or more towing a unit over 10,000 pounds
choice_b: Any vehicle designed to carry more than 15 passengers only
choice_c: A single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 pounds or more, or such a vehicle towing a unit not exceeding 10,000 pounds GVWR
choice_d: Any vehicle requiring hazardous material placards
explanation: Class B is any single vehicle with a GVWR of 26,001 pounds or more, or such a vehicle towing a unit not in excess of 10,000 pounds GVWR.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, Definitions of Classes

question: A Class C license is only considered a commercial driver's license when:
choice_b: The driver is towing a unit over 10,000 pounds
choice_c: It carries an endorsement, such as one for passenger vehicles or hazardous materials
choice_d: The vehicle is registered under the International Registration Plan
explanation: Class C covers vehicles that do not meet the Class A or B definitions; it is a CDL only if it carries an endorsement under 29-A MRSA Section 1253, subsection 3.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, Definitions of Classes

question: What driving privilege does a Maine Class A CDL, with appropriate endorsements, grant to its holder?
choice_a: Operation of Class A vehicles only
choice_b: Operation of any noncommercial vehicle without further testing
choice_c: Operation of all vehicles in Class B and Class C
choice_d: Operation of Class B vehicles only, not Class C
explanation: The manual states a Class A CDL with appropriate endorsements allows operation in all of the other classes (B and C).
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, Change of Class, Restriction, or Endorsement

question: A Class B CDL holder with appropriate endorsements may operate:
choice_a: No other class of vehicle without a new application
choice_b: All vehicles in both Class A and Class C
choice_c: Only the specific Class B vehicle listed on the license
choice_d: All vehicles in Class C, but not Class A vehicles
explanation: A Class B CDL with appropriate endorsements allows operation in all classes except Class A.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, Change of Class, Restriction, or Endorsement

question: Under Maine law, a CDL is required for any vehicle designed to transport how many passengers, including the driver?
explanation: The manual requires a CDL for any vehicle designed to carry more than 15 passengers including the driver, restated elsewhere as 16 or more passengers.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, Do You Need a CDL / Figure 1.1

question: What is the minimum age to operate a Commercial Motor Vehicle in Maine, per the manual's front-matter licensing rules?
explanation: The manual states you must be at least 16 years of age to operate a Commercial Motor Vehicle.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, How to Apply for a Commercial Driver's License

question: What is the minimum age required to operate a bus or transport hazardous materials under a Maine CDL?
explanation: While the general CMV minimum age is 16, the manual specifically requires drivers to be 21 years of age to operate a bus or carry hazardous materials.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, How to Apply for a Commercial Driver's License

question: Effective February 7, 2022, the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration implemented a new regulation requiring what for new CDL applicants and those upgrading an existing CDL?
choice_c: A TSA background check for every CDL class
explanation: The manual notes the FMCSA's ELDT regulation, effective February 7, 2022, requires driver training for new CDL operators and those upgrading their CDL.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, Entry Level Driver Training (ELDT)

question: According to the manual, federal regulations prohibit what during CDL knowledge examinations?
choice_b: Retaking the test after a failed attempt
choice_d: Testing on any day other than Monday
explanation: The manual states federal regulations prohibit the use of interpreters when taking CDL knowledge examinations.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, front matter notice

question: The "N" endorsement on a Maine CDL authorizes the operation of:
explanation: The manual lists the N endorsement as authorizing the operation of tank vehicles only.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, Endorsement

question: The "H" endorsement authorizes operation of vehicles carrying:
choice_a: Liquid cargo in a tank of 119 gallons or more
choice_b: More than 15 passengers including the driver
choice_d: Hazardous material required to be placarded by federal DOT regulation
explanation: The H endorsement is for operation of vehicles carrying hazardous material when required to be placarded by Federal DOT regulation.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, Endorsement

question: The "X" endorsement combines which two other endorsements into one?
explanation: The manual explains that the X endorsement is for tank vehicles carrying hazardous materials, combining the N and H endorsements into one.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, Endorsement

question: The manual notes that the "T" endorsement covers double/triple trailers where allowed by law. Which configuration does the manual specifically state is NOT allowed in Maine?
explanation: The manual states the T endorsement is for double/triple trailers where allowed by law, with a parenthetical note that triple trailers are not allowed in Maine.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, Endorsement

question: Which group of endorsements is awarded upon successful completion of the knowledge examination alone, without a skills test?
choice_c: All six endorsements require a skills test
explanation: The manual states the N, H, X, and T endorsements are awarded upon successful completion of the knowledge examination only; the remaining endorsements (P and S) require the complete test including skills testing.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, Endorsement

question: The "P" endorsement is required to operate passenger vehicles designed to transport:
choice_b: Any number of passengers for hire, regardless of vehicle size
explanation: The P endorsement is for operation of passenger vehicles designed to transport over 15 passengers including the driver.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, Endorsement

question: Successfully qualifying for the "S" (school bus) endorsement also automatically earns which other endorsement, without an additional fee or further examination?
explanation: The manual states successful qualification for the S endorsement will also earn the P endorsement without an additional fee or further examination.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, Endorsement

question: A school bus designed to transport 15 passengers or fewer, including the driver, is associated with which endorsement code on a noncommercial license, rather than requiring a CDL?
explanation: Per the School Bus Endorsement Codes section, a bus designed to transport 15 passengers or fewer including the driver receives endorsement code "Z" on the operator's (noncommercial) license, not a CDL.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, School Bus Endorsement Codes

question: What happens if an applicant does not qualify on the air brake knowledge test or does not take the skills test in an air-brake-equipped vehicle?
choice_a: The applicant is limited to Class C vehicles only
choice_b: The CDL application is denied entirely
choice_c: An air brake restriction is placed on the CDL, prohibiting the driver from operating an air-brake-equipped vehicle
choice_d: The applicant must wait one year before reapplying for any CDL
explanation: The manual explains that failing to qualify on the air brake knowledge and skills components results in an air brake restriction prohibiting operation of air-brake-equipped vehicles.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, Operation of Vehicles Equipped With Air Brakes Not Allowed Restriction

topic: Change of Class, Restriction, or Endorsement
question: To change license class, add an endorsement, or remove a restriction, a Maine CDL holder must:
choice_a: Apply and qualify on the knowledge examination, vision screening, and required skills test
choice_b: Simply request the change online with no additional testing
choice_d: Wait until the next scheduled license renewal date
explanation: The manual requires an applicant changing class, adding an endorsement, or removing a restriction to apply and qualify on the knowledge examination, vision screening, and be issued a learner's permit before qualifying on the skills test.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, Change of Class

question: What is the minimum visual acuity required for a Maine CDL applicant, as screened by the examiner?
explanation: The manual states the minimum visual acuity is a distance rating of 20/40 with the best eye.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, Vision Requirements

question: What is the minimum total field of vision required for a Maine CDL applicant?
explanation: The manual requires a field of vision total of at least 110 degrees.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, Vision Requirements

question: If an applicant meets the visual requirements only while wearing glasses or contact lenses, what is the result?
choice_a: No restriction is noted on the license
choice_b: The applicant must reapply for vision screening every 90 days
choice_c: The permit and operator's license are restricted to corrective lenses
choice_d: The applicant is disqualified from CDL testing entirely
explanation: The manual states that if the visual requirements are met with glasses or contact lenses, the permit and operator's license will be restricted to corrective lenses.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, Vision Requirements

question: Under Maine's learner's permit limitations, how long must the accompanying licensed operator have held a valid license?
explanation: The manual requires the accompanying operator to have held a valid license for two years.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, Limitations of the Learner's Permit

question: What is the minimum age required for the licensed operator accompanying a learner's permit holder, unless the vehicle is a bus or school bus?
explanation: The manual requires the accompanying operator to be at least 20 years of age, or at least 22 if the vehicle is a bus or school bus.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, Limitations of the Learner's Permit

question: If the vehicle being driven under a learner's permit is a bus or school bus, what is the minimum age required for the accompanying licensed operator?
explanation: The manual specifies the accompanying operator must be at least 22 years of age if the vehicle being driven is a bus or school bus.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, Limitations of the Learner's Permit

question: Besides holding the correct license class and being of minimum age, where must the accompanying operator be positioned while a learner's permit holder drives?
choice_a: Anywhere in the vehicle, including a sleeper berth
choice_c: Occupying a seat beside the driver
choice_d: In a separate escort vehicle following behind
explanation: The manual requires the accompanying licensed operator to be occupying a seat beside the driver.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, Limitations of the Learner's Permit

question: How does an applicant schedule a Maine CDL skills test after receiving a learner's permit?
choice_a: By scheduling online through a private third-party vendor
choice_b: By calling the local municipal office directly
choice_c: The skills test is scheduled automatically upon passing the knowledge test
choice_d: By mailing the skills test request card to the Bureau of Motor Vehicles in Augusta
explanation: The manual instructs applicants to mail the skill test request card to the Bureau of Motor Vehicles in Augusta to be scheduled for skills testing.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, How Do I Schedule A Skills Test?

question: What penalty applies if an applicant fails to notify the CDL Examination Section of a skills test appointment cancellation within 48 hours?
choice_b: A $70.00 penalty fee must be paid before another date is scheduled
explanation: The manual states that failing to notify the CDL examination section of a cancellation within 48 hours results in a $70.00 penalty fee before another date is scheduled.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, How Do I Schedule A Skills Test?

question: According to the manual, which type of vehicle may NOT be used for CDL skills test road testing?
choice_b: A vehicle equipped with air brakes
choice_c: A rental vehicle with written permission to substitute a photocopy of the registration
choice_d: A vehicle placarded for hazardous materials
explanation: The manual states that vehicles placarded for hazardous materials may not be used for road testing purposes.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, Definitions of Classes / skills testing requirements

question: What fee must a hazardous materials endorsement applicant pay to the TSA agent for the fingerprint/background records check?
explanation: The manual states the fees associated with the TSA fingerprint/background records check are $89.25, paid to the TSA agent.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, Notification of Security Threat Assessment

question: To be eligible for a hazardous materials endorsement (HME), an applicant must be one of which of the following?
choice_b: A member of a registered trucking association
choice_c: A U.S. citizen, lawful permanent resident, or otherwise meet specific lawful immigration status requirements
choice_d: A resident of Maine for at least five consecutive years
explanation: The manual lists citizenship/immigration status requirements for an HME applicant, including U.S. citizenship, lawful permanent residency, or specific lawful nonimmigrant/refugee/asylum statuses with valid employment authorization.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, Citizenship or Immigration Status Requirements

question: Which of the following is listed as a permanently disqualifying criminal offense for a hazardous materials endorsement?
choice_c: Filing a late state tax return
explanation: The manual's list of permanently disqualifying criminal offenses for a hazmat endorsement includes espionage, sedition, treason, and certain terrorism- and explosives-related felonies.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, List of Disqualifying Criminal Offenses for Hazardous Materials Endorsement, Part A

question: Under the interim disqualifying offenses list, a driver is disqualified from holding a hazmat endorsement if convicted of an offense like extortion or arson within what time period before the date of application?
choice_b: There is no time limit specified
explanation: Part B of the disqualifying offenses list disqualifies an applicant convicted (or found not guilty by reason of insanity) of an interim disqualifying felony within the previous seven years, or released from prison for one within the last five years.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, List of Disqualifying Criminal Offenses for Hazardous Materials Endorsement, Part B

question: Which knowledge test must be taken by ALL CDL applicants, regardless of the class of license or endorsements sought?
explanation: Section 1.1.1 states the general knowledge test is taken by all applicants, while the other listed tests apply only to specific endorsements or vehicle types.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, 1.1.1 Knowledge Tests

question: The CDL skills test is broken down into which three general types of testing?
choice_a: Pre-trip vehicle inspection, basic vehicle control, and on-road driving
choice_b: Written exam, vision screening, and road test
choice_c: Air brake test, vision test, and road test
choice_d: Backing, parking, and highway driving only
explanation: Section 1.1.2 identifies the three general skills tested as pre-trip inspection, basic vehicle control, and on-road driving.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, 1.1.2 Skills Tests

question: What is the minimum disqualification period for a first offense of operating a CMV with a blood alcohol concentration of .04% or higher?
explanation: Section 1.2.2 states a driver will lose their CDL for at least one year for a first offense of operating a CMV at or above .04% BAC.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, 1.2.2 Alcohol, Leaving the Scene of an Accident, and Commission of a Felony

question: The one-year disqualification for a first alcohol-related offense increases to how long if the offense occurs while operating a CMV placarded for hazardous materials?
explanation: The manual states the disqualification period is at least three years if the offense occurs while operating a CMV placarded for hazardous materials.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, 1.2.2 Alcohol, Leaving the Scene of an Accident, and Commission of a Felony

question: What is the disqualification consequence for a second offense involving BAC, refusal to test, or a CMV-related felony?
choice_b: A $5,000 fine with no license impact
explanation: The manual states a driver will lose their CDL for life for a second qualifying offense.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, 1.2.2 Alcohol, Leaving the Scene of an Accident, and Commission of a Felony

question: Which of the following is defined by the manual as a "serious traffic violation" for CDL purposes?
choice_b: Excessive speeding of 15 mph or more above the posted limit
explanation: Section 1.2.3 defines serious traffic violations to include excessive speeding of 15 mph or more above the posted limit, along with reckless driving and other listed offenses.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, 1.2.3 Serious Traffic Violations

question: What is the minimum CDL disqualification period for committing two serious traffic violations within a three-year period?
explanation: Section 1.2.3 states a driver loses their CDL for at least 60 days for two serious traffic violations within a three-year period, and at least 120 days for three or more.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, 1.2.3 Serious Traffic Violations

question: What is the minimum disqualification period for a first violation of an out-of-service order?
explanation: Section 1.2.4 states a driver loses their CDL for at least 90 days for a first violation of an out-of-service order.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, 1.2.4 Violation of Out-of-Service Orders

question: What is the minimum CDL disqualification period for a first railroad-highway grade crossing violation?
explanation: Section 1.2.5 states a driver loses their CDL for at least 60 days for a first railroad-highway grade crossing violation, escalating to 120 days for a second within three years and one year for a third.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, 1.2.5 Railroad-highway Grade Crossing Violations

question: If a CDL holder's privilege to operate their personal vehicle is revoked, cancelled, or suspended due to an alcohol, controlled substance, or felony violation, what happens to their CDL?
choice_a: They lose their CDL driving privileges for 1 year
choice_b: They lose their CDL for only 30 days
choice_c: They must only retake the vision screening
choice_d: There is no effect on their CDL
explanation: Section 1.2.7 states that if a CDL holder's personal vehicle privilege is revoked, cancelled, or suspended due to alcohol, controlled substance, or felony violations, they lose their CDL for 1 year; a second such violation results in lifetime loss.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, 1.2.7 Traffic Violations in Your Personal Vehicle

question: Under the other CDL rules described in the manual, a CDL holder may not:
choice_a: Operate a CMV registered under the International Registration Plan
choice_b: Have more than one driver's license
choice_c: Drive a CMV that has been apportioned under IFTA
choice_d: Change endorsements more than once per calendar year
explanation: Section 1.3 states a driver cannot have more than one license; breaking this rule can result in a court fine of up to $5,000 or jail time.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, 1.3 Other CDL Rules

question: A CDL holder must notify their employer of a conviction for any traffic violation (except parking) within how many days?
explanation: Section 1.3 requires a CDL holder to notify their employer within 30 days of conviction for any traffic violation, except parking, no matter what type of vehicle was being driven.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, 1.3 Other CDL Rules

question: A CDL holder must notify their employer within how many business days if their license is suspended, revoked, canceled, or they are disqualified from driving?
choice_c: There is no specific timeframe given
explanation: Section 1.3 requires notification to the employer within two business days of a suspension, revocation, cancellation, or disqualification.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, 1.3 Other CDL Rules

question: According to the manual, a CMV driver who does not wear a safety belt is how many times more likely to be fatally injured if thrown from the vehicle?
choice_d: The manual states there is no increased risk
explanation: Section 1.3 states that a driver who does not wear a safety belt is four times more likely to be fatally injured if thrown from the vehicle.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, 1.3 Other CDL Rules

question: For the school bus pre-trip equipment check portion of the SKILLS test, what percentage of items must an applicant properly check to qualify?
choice_a: 100% of the items included in the check
choice_b: 50% of the items included in the check
choice_c: 80% of the items included in the check
choice_d: 60% of the items included in the check
explanation: This 80% figure is a scoring standard for the hands-on pre-trip equipment check during the SKILLS test, not the passing percentage or item count for the separate written knowledge test.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Manual (2005 CDL Testing System base AAMVA content, Maine revision 7/24), Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 1, Introduction, Pre-Trip Equipment Check (School Bus Operator's Examination)

question: The modernized CDL Skills Exam standard, developed by AAMVA, was approved by the Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration (FMCSA) on what date?
explanation: The Addendum states the new AAMVA CDL Skills Exam standard was approved by the FMCSA on August 11, 2022.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Skills Test Addendum, Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Modernized CDL Skills Exam Standard transition

question: According to the Addendum, on what date will Maine begin transitioning to the new Vehicle Inspection (VI) standard for CDL skills exam applicants?
explanation: The Addendum states Maine will begin using the new Vehicle Inspection modeling starting November 1, 2026, for applicants scheduled for a full CDL Skills Exam on or after that date.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Skills Test Addendum, Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Transition to modernized Vehicle Inspection standard

question: When will Maine fully transition to all of the new modernized CDL skills exam standards, including the Basic Control Skills test?
explanation: The Addendum states Maine will transition fully to all the new modernized standards on September 1, 2027, at which point the addendum itself becomes void.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Skills Test Addendum, Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Full transition to modernized standards

question: Per the Addendum, how is the 90-minute full CDL Skills Exam divided?
choice_a: Four segments of approximately 22 minutes each
choice_b: Three segments of 30 minutes each: Vehicle Inspection, Basic Control Skills, and Road Test
choice_d: One continuous 90-minute road test with no separate segments
explanation: The Addendum states the time allotted for each of the three segments of the exam is 30 minutes, for a total of 90 minutes for a full CDL Skills Exam.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Skills Test Addendum, Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- What is not changing (exam segment timing)

topic: What Remains Unchanged in the Transition
question: Which portion of the CDL Skills Exam does the Addendum specifically state remains the same throughout Maine's transition to the modernized standard?
choice_c: The Basic Control Skills maneuver list
explanation: The Addendum states that the public Road Test segment remained the same under the new AAMVA standard and remains unchanged during Maine's transition.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Skills Test Addendum, Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- What is not changing (Road Test)

question: Until what date will Maine continue conducting Basic Control Skills testing using the four maneuvers outlined in the Addendum?
choice_a: The Addendum states there is no planned change
explanation: The Addendum states Maine will continue Basic Control Skills testing with the four maneuvers outlined in the addendum until September 1, 2027, after which the addendum becomes void.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Skills Test Addendum, Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Basic Control Skills transition timeline

question: According to the Addendum, what is one key change to the Vehicle Inspection portion under the modernized standard?
choice_a: The Vehicle Inspection segment is eliminated entirely
choice_b: Fewer items need to be inspected, with a focus on critical safety items
choice_c: A written exam replaces the physical inspection demonstration
choice_d: The Vehicle Inspection time is extended to 60 minutes
explanation: The Addendum states the modernized Vehicle Inspection has fewer items to inspect, with a focus on critical safety items, along with a new applicant checklist.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Skills Test Addendum, Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Changes to the Vehicle Inspection

question: Which four exercises make up the Basic Control Skills test described in the Addendum?
choice_a: Pre-trip inspection, road test, backing, and parking
choice_c: Parallel park, three-point turn, hill start, and lane change
choice_d: Straight line backing, forward through offset alley, reverse offset/parallel park, and alley dock
explanation: The Addendum's Section 12 lists straight line backing, forward through offset alley, parallel park (conventional/reverse offset), and alley dock as the four off-road exercises.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Skills Test Addendum, Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 12, Basic Vehicle Control Skills Test

question: For passenger (bus) or school bus endorsement skills testing, which maneuver replaces the standard alley dock exercise?
explanation: The Addendum states the alley dock is not a representative maneuver for a bus, so maneuver #4 for passenger and school bus endorsements is a bus turnaround instead.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Skills Test Addendum, Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 12, Maneuver #4 Bus Turnaround

question: Under the Basic Control Skills scoring criteria described in the Addendum, what is scored as a "pull-up"?
choice_a: When a driver stops and reverses direction to get a better position
choice_b: Touching a cone during the exercise
choice_c: Exiting the vehicle to check its position
choice_d: Any time the vehicle comes to a complete stop
explanation: The Addendum defines a pull-up as when a driver stops and reverses direction to get a better position; stopping without changing direction does not count as a pull-up.
source_note: Maine Commercial Driver License Skills Test Addendum, Maine Secretary of State / Bureau of Motor Vehicles -- Section 12, 12.1 Scoring

question: According to the Addendum, does Maine's transition to the modernized skills exam standard change the Entry Level Driver Training (ELDT) requirements?
choice_a: Yes, ELDT is eliminated for Class B applicants
choice_b: Yes, required ELDT training hours are doubled
choice_c: Yes, ELDT now requires a separate TSA background check
choice_d: No, ELDT requirements under 49 CFR Part 380 Appendices A-E remain unchanged
explanation: The Addendum lists as "not changing" the ELDT requirements under 49 CFR Part 380 Appendices A-E for training provider curriculums.
